subject: Civil Engineering
title: Tunnel Ventilation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tunnel Ventilation usable.

hook.text: Air doesn't flow underground. Without ventilation, a road tunnel fills with deadly exhaust.

buildup.text: Longitudinal ventilation uses jet fans mounted on the ceiling — pushing air in one direction.

discovery.text: Transverse ventilation uses dedicated air ducts — fresh air in one, exhaust out another.

twist.text: Fire changes everything — smoke must be controlled to keep escape routes clear.

climax.text: The Mont Blanc tunnel fire killed 39 in 1999 — ventilation redesign followed worldwide.

punchline.text: Ventilation keeps people breathing — and in a fire, it decides who escapes.

quiz.question: Why did the 1999 Mont Blanc tunnel fire lead to global ventilation redesigns?
options: The fire was caused by a faulty ventilation system
Inadequate smoke control trapped motorists — 39 people died, proving ventilation is life-critical
The tunnel's fans accelerated the fire beyond control

details.summary: Tunnel ventilation systems provide fresh air, dilute vehicle exhaust and smoke, and control air temperature using longitudinal, transverse, or semi-transverse airflow systems.
details.whyItMatters: Ventilation is the most critical life safety system in road tunnels. The catastrophic Mont Blanc tunnel fire in 1999 killed 39 people largely because smoke could not be controlled, transforming ventilation standards worldwide.
takeaways: Longitudinal ventilation uses jet fans to push air through the tunnel in one direction
Transverse ventilation supplies and exhausts air through separate overhead ducts
Fire ventilation must control smoke to maintain tenable conditions for evacuation

faq.question: How do jet fans control air flow in a tunnel?
faq.answer: Jet fans are high-velocity axial fans mounted on the tunnel ceiling that push air in one direction by momentum transfer. In normal operation they dilute vehicle emissions.

faq.question: Why did the Mont Blanc tunnel fire change ventilation design worldwide?
faq.answer: The fire burned for two days, killing 39 people trapped in smoke that the semi-transverse ventilation could not control. Investigations revealed inadequate emergency ventilation capacity and operational procedures.
